# HRV recording fixtures

Synthetic, deterministic, seeded RR-interval recordings used for differential
regression testing of the analysis engine. They contain no identifiable or
real-world data.

## Contents

| Fixture | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `clean-normal` | Clean recording with normal respiratory and LF variation |
| `high-vagal-variation` | Large respiratory (HF) oscillation |
| `low-variability` | Near-constant intervals (very low HRV) |
| `respiratory-hf-dominant` | Dominant HF band |
| `lf-dominant` | Dominant LF band |
| `slow-hr-drift` | Gradual heart-rate drift across the recording |
| `single-ectopic` | One extra beat detection |
| `multiple-ectopics` | Eight extra beat detections (still usable) |
| `missed-detection` | One doubled interval (missed detection) |
| `extra-detection` | Extra beat with compensatory pause |
| `short-signal-gap` | A single 2.5 s gap (correctable, below the signal-loss threshold) |
| `borderline-poor` | 22 ectopic beats (>5% and >20 beats) — must be rejected |

## Reference outputs

Each fixture stores `expected` reference outputs. These were generated by the
current engine baseline and lock the implementation against regressions: any
engine change that alters output for an unchanged input fails the differential
test.

**Important:** these values are **not yet independently validated** against
Kubios or the DanFunD analysis pipeline. External parity validation is a
separate exercise; until then these fixtures catch internal regressions only.

## Regenerating

```bash
bun run scripts/generate-hrv-fixtures.ts
```

Only regenerate when the engine behaviour intentionally changes, and review the
diff of the reference outputs before committing.
